doc.title: Bob Hardaway interviewed by Monk Rowe, Los Angeles, California, February 14, 1999

chapter: Ray Anthony and the big band end
title: Arriving at the end of the big band era; ghost bands; Ray Anthony and Sy Zentner
summary: He reached big bands at the very end, before ghost bands and tribute bands took over. His first name band was Ray Anthony around 1951-52, then Sy Zentner.

story.theme_name: Getting paid: wages, tips and leaving over money
story.community_name: Quitting the band: why sidemen left

blocks.x: So you got into big bands when the big band era had had its real popular run.
But it was still going on enough that you could find work.
Yeah, there were still some ballrooms, and this was before the era of every band was a ghost band. Every band has a ghost leader now and maybe more than one.

How many Benny Goodman’s Tributes have there been? They can’t say the Benny Goodman Band, but they have to say a “Tribute” to, I’m sure Abe told you that. He just did one in Japan recently. But there were still some bands. The first so-called name band, I played with a few bands, panic sort of bands. The first name band I played with was Ray Anthony. And I think it was ’51, I think. I lost track a little bit, but it was either ’51 or ’52. That’s close enough. And he was very hot at the time. He was about the last one that made it. One of the other bands that made it for a while, it didn’t last as long as Ray, was Sy Zentner got a band and I was on that band as well. But the rest of the bands were just rehashing the Glenn Miller and Tommy Dorsey and things.
